---
title: "Cranberry Models: Common Control"
output: html_document
params:
  data_file: "acute_yield_data_fall_2026.csv"
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo=TRUE, message=FALSE)
library(nlme)
```

## Data

All Control observations share one treatment category. Original plot pairs are retained.
Pooling assumes the control protocols and pulse schedules have no important group-specific effects.

```{r data}
data_clean <- read.csv(params$data_file)
data_clean$year <- factor(data_clean$year)
data_clean$cultivar <- factor(toupper(trimws(data_clean$cultivar)))
data_clean$intensity_group <- factor(toupper(trimws(data_clean$intensity_group)))
data_clean$treatment <- factor(
  toupper(trimws(data_clean$treatment)), levels=c("CONTROL", "OTC")
)

# Define pairs BEFORE pooling the controls.
data_clean$pair_id <- with(data_clean,
  interaction(year, cultivar, intensity_group, plot, drop=TRUE)
)
stopifnot(!anyNA(data_clean$treatment))
stopifnot(all(table(data_clean$pair_id, data_clean$treatment) == 1))

data_clean$heat_group <- with(data_clean,
  ifelse(treatment == "CONTROL", "Control", as.character(intensity_group))
)
data_clean$heat_group <- factor(
  data_clean$heat_group, levels=c("Control", "A", "B", "C", "D")
)
stopifnot(!anyNA(data_clean$heat_group))

data_clean$total_weight <- with(data_clean, healthy_weight + rotten_weight)
stopifnot(all(data_clean$total_weight > 0),
          all(data_clean$healthy_n + data_clean$rotten_n > 0))
data_clean$healthy_count_pct <- with(data_clean,
  100 * healthy_n / (healthy_n + rotten_n)
)
data_clean$healthy_weight_pct <- with(data_clean,
  100 * healthy_weight / total_weight
)
with(data_clean, table(year, cultivar, heat_group))
```

## Model 1: Total fruit weight

```{r total}
m_total <- lme(
  total_weight ~ year * cultivar + heat_group,
  random=~1 | pair_id,
  data=data_clean, method="ML",
  control=lmeControl(opt="optim")
)
summary(m_total)
anova(m_total, type="marginal")
```

## Model 2: Healthy fruit weight

```{r healthy}
m_healthy <- lme(
  healthy_weight ~ year * cultivar + heat_group,
  random=~1 | pair_id,
  data=data_clean, method="ML",
  control=lmeControl(opt="optim")
)
summary(m_healthy)
anova(m_healthy, type="marginal")
```

## Model 3: Healthy percentage by count

```{r count-rate}
m_count_pct <- lme(
  healthy_count_pct ~ year * cultivar + heat_group,
  random=~1 | pair_id,
  data=data_clean, method="ML",
  control=lmeControl(opt="optim")
)
summary(m_count_pct)
anova(m_count_pct, type="marginal")
```

## Model 4: Healthy percentage by weight

```{r weight-rate}
m_weight_pct <- lme(
  healthy_weight_pct ~ year * cultivar + heat_group,
  random=~1 | pair_id,
  data=data_clean, method="ML",
  control=lmeControl(opt="optim")
)
summary(m_weight_pct)
anova(m_weight_pct, type="marginal")
```

## A-D versus the common Control

In the additive models, heat_group coefficients are adjusted A-D minus Control
differences, assumed common across years and cultivars. Weights are in grams;
healthy percentage differences are in percentage points. Intervals are pointwise.
Holm p values are adjusted across the four contrasts within each response.

```{r contrasts}
models <- list(total_weight=m_total, healthy_weight=m_healthy,
               healthy_count_pct=m_count_pct, healthy_weight_pct=m_weight_pct)
effects <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(models), function(name) {
  fit <- models[[name]]
  tab <- summary(fit)$tTable
  tab <- tab[grepl("^heat_group", rownames(tab)), , drop=FALSE]
  data.frame(outcome=name,
    comparison=paste(sub("heat_group", "", rownames(tab)), "- Control"),
    estimate=tab[, "Value"],
    lower=tab[, "Value"] - qt(.975, tab[, "DF"]) * tab[, "Std.Error"],
    upper=tab[, "Value"] + qt(.975, tab[, "DF"]) * tab[, "Std.Error"],
    p_value=tab[, "p-value"],
    p_holm=p.adjust(tab[, "p-value"], method="holm"), row.names=NULL)
}))
knitr::kable(effects, digits=4)
```

## Does the heat response differ between cultivars?

These candidate models retain a common Control category but allow the A-D effects
to vary by cultivar. Compare fixed effects using ML; do not automatically select
a model based on one p value.

```{r cultivar-interaction}
m_total_cultivar <- update(m_total, . ~ . + heat_group:cultivar)
m_healthy_cultivar <- update(m_healthy, . ~ . + heat_group:cultivar)
m_count_pct_cultivar <- update(m_count_pct, . ~ . + heat_group:cultivar)
m_weight_pct_cultivar <- update(m_weight_pct, . ~ . + heat_group:cultivar)

anova(m_total, m_total_cultivar)
anova(m_healthy, m_healthy_cultivar)
anova(m_count_pct, m_count_pct_cultivar)
anova(m_weight_pct, m_weight_pct_cultivar)
```

## Intensity comparisons: A-D

A, B, C and D correspond to 4, 3, 2 and 1 heat pulses.
Weight outcomes use the cultivar-interaction models; percentage outcomes use
additive models. Means are averaged equally over years (and cultivars for
percentage outcomes). Controls remain pooled within each year and cultivar.
Comparisons use Holm correction for the six A-D pairs within each outcome/cultivar;
confidence intervals are pointwise 95%, not simultaneous. Degrees of freedom
use a conservative minimum over the fixed coefficients involved.

```{r intensity-helper}
# No additional packages are required.
intensity_results <- function(fit, cultivar_level=NULL) {
  grid <- expand.grid(
    year=levels(data_clean$year),
    cultivar=if (is.null(cultivar_level)) levels(data_clean$cultivar) else cultivar_level,
    heat_group=levels(data_clean$heat_group)
  )
  grid$year <- factor(grid$year, levels=levels(data_clean$year))
  grid$cultivar <- factor(grid$cultivar, levels=levels(data_clean$cultivar))
  grid$heat_group <- factor(grid$heat_group, levels=levels(data_clean$heat_group))
  X <- model.matrix(delete.response(terms(formula(fit))), grid)
  X <- X[, names(fixef(fit)), drop=FALSE]
  mean_X <- do.call(rbind, lapply(levels(data_clean$heat_group), function(g) {
    colMeans(X[grid$heat_group == g, , drop=FALSE])
  }))
  rownames(mean_X) <- levels(data_clean$heat_group)

  estimate_contrast <- function(L) {
    estimate <- as.numeric(L %*% fixef(fit))
    se <- sqrt(as.numeric(L %*% vcov(fit) %*% L))
    df <- min(fit$fixDF$X[abs(L) > 1e-10])
    data.frame(estimate=estimate, SE=se, df=df,
      lower=estimate-qt(.975,df)*se,
      upper=estimate+qt(.975,df)*se,
      p_value=2*pt(-abs(estimate/se),df))
  }
  means <- do.call(rbind, lapply(rownames(mean_X), function(g) {
    cbind(group=g, estimate_contrast(mean_X[g, ]))
  }))
  # Pairwise comparisons ONLY among heated groups.
  pairs <- combn(c("A", "B", "C", "D"), 2, simplify=FALSE)
  comparisons <- do.call(rbind, lapply(pairs, function(g) {
    cbind(comparison=paste(g, collapse=" - "),
      estimate_contrast(mean_X[g[1], ] - mean_X[g[2], ]))
  }))
  comparisons$p_holm <- p.adjust(comparisons$p_value, method="holm")
  list(means=means, comparisons=comparisons)
}

# A-D scheme effects relative to the common Control can also be compared
# by subtracting each scheme's mean_X row from another, as above:
# (A - Control) - (B - Control) = A - B.
```

```{r intensity-tables-plots, results='asis', fig.width=8, fig.height=5}
intensity_models <- list(
  total_weight=m_total_cultivar,
  healthy_weight=m_healthy_cultivar,
  healthy_count_pct=m_count_pct,
  healthy_weight_pct=m_weight_pct
)
intensity_export <- list()

for (outcome in names(intensity_models)) {
  fit <- intensity_models[[outcome]]
  is_weight <- outcome %in% c("total_weight", "healthy_weight")
  groups <- if (is_weight) levels(data_clean$cultivar) else "Both cultivars"
  for (g in groups) {
    result <- intensity_results(fit, if (is_weight) g else NULL)
    cat("\n\n### ", outcome, ": ", g, "\n\n", sep="")
    # A mean-vs-zero p value is not relevant here, so omit it.
    print(knitr::kable(result$means[c("group","estimate","SE","lower","upper")],
      digits=2, caption="Adjusted means and pointwise 95% confidence intervals"))
    cat("\n\n")
    print(knitr::kable(result$comparisons, digits=4,
      caption="A-D comparisons; negative estimates mean the first group is lower"))
    cat("\n\n")

    # Order the plot by pulse count: Control, D, C, B, A.
    z <- result$means[match(c("Control","D","C","B","A"),result$means$group), ]
    plot(0:4, z$estimate, type="b", pch=19, xaxt="n",
      ylim=range(z$lower,z$upper), xlab="Heat pulses",
      ylab=if (is_weight) "Adjusted weight (g)" else "Adjusted healthy percentage (%)",
      main=paste(outcome,g))
    axis(1, at=0:4, labels=c("Control","D: 1","C: 2","B: 3","A: 4"))
    arrows(0:4,z$lower,0:4,z$upper,angle=90,code=3,length=.05)
    # Lines guide the eye; the model treats pulse schemes as categories.
    intensity_export[[paste(outcome,g)]] <- list(means=result$means,
                                                comparisons=result$comparisons)
  }
}
```

Pulse timing also differs across A-D; these are scheme comparisons, not a
confirmed causal effect per additional pulse. The connecting lines do not imply
a fitted linear trend. Control has no active heating; its chamber protocol is
assumed comparable across the original intensity groups.

## Diagnostics

```{r diagnostics, fig.width=9, fig.height=4}
models <- intensity_models
for (name in names(models)) {
  fit <- models[[name]]
  r <- residuals(fit, type="normalized")
  par(mfrow=c(1,2))
  plot(fitted(fit), r, xlab="Fitted", ylab="Normalized residual", main=name)
  abline(h=0, lty=2)
  qqnorm(r); qqline(r)
}
par(mfrow=c(1,1))
```

These are preliminary Gaussian mixed models. Percentage responses require
particular care with residual variance, normality and predictions outside 0-100.
Consider beta-binomial (count percentage) or beta (weight percentage) models if needed.
Cultivar is confounded with field; year effects do not identify a weather or alternate-bearing mechanism.
